title: Local rings of a normal integral curve are principal ideal domains
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $Y$ be a curve over $k$ [def-pc-curve], meaning a separated integral scheme of finite type over $k$ and dimension one. Assume $Y$ is normal: every local ring is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. For every point $y\in Y$, the local ring $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is Noetherian (each ideal is finitely generated) [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and has Krull dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. If $\dim A=0$, then $A$ is a field; if $\dim A=1$, then $A$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. These are the only cases. In particular, for every $y\in Y$, $A$ is a principal ideal domain: an integral domain in which every ideal is generated by a single element.

source.place: Tag 0CCK, lemma-flat, proof, first sentence (field or DVR), citing varieties.tex Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve, and algebra.tex Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr. proof.text: Every ideal of the field $k$ is either $(0)$ or $(1)$: a nonzero element of an ideal has its inverse in $k$, so the ideal contains $1$. Thus $k$ is Noetherian. The one affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}k$ therefore makes this base locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The structure morphism of the curve $Y$ is of finite type, hence locally of finite type, by [def-pc-curve]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to conclude that $Y$ is locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian, applied over a field; Properties Tag 01OV, definition-noetherian

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$. Choose an affine open neighbourhood $U$ of $y$ with $R=\mathcal O_Y(U)$ Noetherian, using the covering definition [pqf-def-locnoeth]. By clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the germ map $R\to A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a localization at $R\setminus\mathfrak p_y$. This is a multiplicative subset because $\mathfrak p_y$ is prime. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] to this germ map. It follows that $A$ is Noetherian.

Normality gives that $A$ is a nonzero integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Since $Y$ is a scheme, its structure-sheaf stalk $A$ is a local ring [def-pc-scheme]. By [def-pc-curve] and [def-pc-dimension], $1=\dim Y=\sup_{z\in Y}\dim\mathcal O_{Y,z}$, so $\dim A\leq1$. The prime ideal $(0)$ of the domain $A$ gives a chain of length zero, hence $\dim A\geq0$. The chain-length definition [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] now leaves exactly $\dim A=0$ or $\dim A=1$.

source.place: Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve, local dimension input; dimension bound directly from the local-ring supremum convention

proof.text: If $\dim A=0$, let $\mathfrak m_y$ be its maximal ideal. A maximal ideal is prime: if $ab\in\mathfrak m_y$ and $a\notin\mathfrak m_y$, maximality gives $1=ta+c$ with $c\in\mathfrak m_y$, so $b=tab+cb\in\mathfrak m_y$. Thus $\mathfrak m_y\neq(0)$ would give the strict prime chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak m_y$ of length one, contradicting [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Hence $\mathfrak m_y=(0)$. By [def-weil-residue-field], $A/\mathfrak m_y=\kappa(y)$ is a field; the map $a\mapsto[a]$ identifies $A=A/(0)$ with this field.

source.place: Tag 0CCK, lemma-flat, first sentence: the field case, written out

proof.text: If $\dim A=1$, the preceding steps give all the hypotheses of [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr]: $A$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain. Its conclusion says precisely that $A$ is a discrete valuation ring. This application needs neither perfection of $k$ nor separability of any residue field.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, (5) implies (1); Varieties Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve

proof.text: In the dimension-zero case, every ideal of the field $A$ is $(0)$ or $(1)$, by the inverse argument of step 1. In the dimension-one case, every ideal of $A$ is principal by the discrete valuation ring definition [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Since $A$ is a domain in both cases, it is a principal ideal domain. Together with steps 2--5 this proves every asserted clause for the arbitrary point $y$.
